findings.reason: I confirmed that `new_from_params` assigns the raw email and that `should_block?` does an exact `where(email:)` match, so changing the case or adding whitespace gets past a blocked entry; it is a real bypass but a narrow one.

`UsersController#create` runs `user.valid?` on every request, because it is evaluated before the `&&`, and then calls `user.save`; on a new record `email_changed?` is true both times, so the side-effecting `should_block?` adds 2 to match_count per attempt (the finding wrongly ties this to the hub setting), though only statistics are affected.
The non-atomic read-modify-write can lose increments under concurrent requests, but this is a minor statistics inaccuracy.

I confirmed that any error under errors.email, including 'has already been taken', adds the address to rejectedEmails and shows the generic 'invalid' reason, which is misleading UX but small because the flash still shows the server message.
The test gap is real: there is no controller spec for the new errors/values keys or for the double count, but it is a non-critical path.
